messages:
Marco: Pasting the QuotaSync renewal offer we got this morning. Need procurement + finance + legal input before I reply. Main ask: better overage terms and a firmer escalator cap. Quote excerpt below.

Marco: ```
Vendor: QuotaSync Inc.
Quote ID: QS-5578-2026
Term: 12 months
Committed: 50,000,000 tokens/month
Current price (we pay today): $0.00080/token
Proposed price: $0.00100/token
Committed discount: 12% off list for 12mo commit (effective $0.00088/token)
Overage rate: $0.00150/token (billed monthly)
Price escalator: vendor reserves right to increase price annually up to 12%
Invoicing: monthly in arrears, Net30
SLA credits: none listed
Data: SOC2 Type II claimed, cert to be provided on request
```

Lina (finance): Quick math: baseline current spend ~50M * 0.0008 = $40k/mo. Proposed (no discount) = $50k/mo. With their 12% commit discount they quote ~$44k/mo — still ~10% higher than today.
Lina (finance): Two red flags: overage @ $0.0015 is steep; escalator up to 12%/yr is unacceptable. Also Net30 is fine but invoice disputes need at least 45-60 day cushion for our AP cycle.

Priya (eng): Are we using QuotaSync for routing/model-serving or just observability? If it's only billing/insights we shouldn't commit full token volumes. Our forecast shows ~20% usage growth next quarter — committing 50M might be tight. Also ask if rates differ by SKU (generation vs embeddings).

Sam (legal): Add DPA + SOC2 evidence before signing. Ask for a cap on annual price increases (recommend 7%). Include audit + change-of-control termination. Need vendor to accept standard Redwood confidentiality & security addendum. Also push for SLA credits tied to availability or invoice errors.

Marco: Proposed counterpoints for us to agree on before I send a reply: 1) Counter: 12mo commit at $0.00095/token (net), 2) Overage capped at 10% of committed tokens billed at $0.00100/token, 3) Escalator cap at 7%/yr, 4) Net45 invoicing + 60-day dispute hold, 5) SOC2 + DPA contractually attached, 6) 30 days of trial credits for any pilot + pro-rata credits for downtime. Thoughts? @Priya @Lina @Sam :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:?

Priya (eng): I can join the vendor call for tech Qs (Wed 10am PT). We should insist on separate SKUs for embeddings vs gen. If they won't split, put a floor on embedding unit pricing. 

Lina (finance): I can handle the pricing counters. Also would like a clause that limits overage exposure to a single invoice (i.e., vendor can't retro-charge older invoices). Net45 is reasonable for us.

Sam (legal): I can redline the DPA + escalator clause. Ask vendor to commit to providing SOC2 report within 7 business days of our request. Also push for termination right if they materially change price or data handling.

Zoe (revops): From GTM perspective, predictable unit cost matters. Longer commit helps us price partner integrations. If we can get the $0.00095 and 10% overage cap I'm okay with committing 12mo. Would prefer ability to scale commit mid-term if usage grows.

Marco: Action items: I'll send counter-offer today by EOD with the points above. Priya to join Wed 10am vendor call. Lina will include spend forecasts to justify scaling clause. Sam will prepare DPA redline.

Marco: Draft reply to vendor (first pass):
Marco: ```
Hi Javier / QuotaSync team,
Thanks for the quote QS-5578-2026. A few items we need clarified/modified before we can proceed: 
- 12mo commit at $0.00095/token (net)
- Overage capped to 10% of committed tokens per month, billed at $0.00100/token
- Annual escalator capped at 7%
- Net45 invoicing, 60-day dispute window
- SOC2 Type II evidence + DPA attached to agreement
- 30 days trial credits for pilot + pro-rata credits for any service downtime
Please let us know if you can accept these terms or propose alternatives. We are happy to schedule a call (Wed 10am PT suggested) to discuss technical SKUs and usage profiles.
Best,
Marco (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
```

Lina (finance): That looks good. Also ask for an itemized invoice template showing committed vs overage lines so we can automate reconciliation.

Priya (eng): Add that call agenda should cover: SKU definitions, throttling behavior, KV cache implications for embedding usage, and any per-model token rounding.

Sam (legal): I'll queue up our DPA redline and circulate internally. If they push back on escalator cap, propose CPI-based adjustments with a ceiling.

Marco: Sending now. I'll post vendor response in this thread when I get it. Thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
